description: The close codes the browser sends when IT ends a hub socket (the store worker's document socket, the shell's directory stream). A browser WebSocket.close(code) accepts only 1000 or a code in 3000..4999 (WHATWG WebSockets, close() step 1) and throws InvalidAccessError otherwise, which leaves the socket open; the protocol-level codes of RFC 6455 section 7.4.1 (1002, 1008, ...) are reserved for the endpoints themselves. So every worker-initiated close uses the private-use range 4000..4999, mapping the RFC meaning into it (4000 + the RFC code's last three digits), with a reason of at most 123 UTF-8 bytes.
